content.text:
The pattern fits Lu4Zr3O12 (mp-1222825) alone. I located peak positions approximately by counting along the intensity grid. I did not compute any candidate patterns; the assignment comes from lattice-geometry estimates.

- **Main peaks:** the strongest feature is a split pair near 30.2° and 30.6° (100 and 86). A second split pair sits near 34.75° and 35.5° (41 and 24). These match fluorite 111 and 200 reflections with a cubic cell of about 5.1 Å (d(111) ≈ 2.95 Å, about 30.3°). The splitting points to a rhombohedral distortion.
- **Superstructure peaks:** weaker peaks at about 14.45°, 18.25°, 22.7° and 24° are consistent with the ordered δ-phase superstructure of Lu4Zr3O12.
- **Higher-angle peaks:** there are also split peaks near 50° and 59–60°, as expected for distorted fluorite 220 and 311.
- **Ba2YTaO6 ruled out:** it is cubic, so it cannot produce the split doublets. Its strong 220 (about 29.6°) and 400 (about 42.3°) peaks do not match. It also has no strong peak near 34.7°. Its 111 peak (about 18.0°) is close to 18.25° but not a match.
- **Monoclinic double perovskites ruled out:** Pr2ZnPtO6 and Sm2MnRhO6 would put their main peak near 31.5° and 32.1°. The observed doublet is at 30.2–30.6°.
- **Other candidates not checked:** I did not individually rule out the SiO2, Sr2Li2Nb3O10, BaAl2Sb2O7, Nb2O5 and CrAuO2 candidates. The observed peaks are all explained by Lu4Zr3O12, so I found no need for a second phase.
